law: Use the XCUIAutomation framework to control your app’s user interface and inspect its state.
Use to write tests that control your app using XCUIAutomation, and check if your app’s state matches your expectations.
You can still use it to test compatible iPad and iPhone apps that you build using the iOS SDK but run in visionOS.
Replicate sequences of interactions and make sure that your app’s user interface behaves as intended.
When you write UI tests with XCUIAutomation, you use to find the elements in your app that your test interacts with.
Use UI recording to replicate your app interactions so that Xcode constructs the element queries for you.
In these situations, you don’t need to launch your app in the test.

For example, if you’re likely to move a given button when redesigning your app’s UI, but the name of the button never changes, choose a query that locates it by name instead of its index in its parent element.
Use element queries to find UI elements, and assertion macros from to assert that the elements have the expected properties.
Use this to test that recorded interactions in your app are still possible in updated versions, and that the app doesn’t crash when you interact with it.
